title: New Jersey Law Against Discrimination source-of-income protection
requirement: A landlord may not discriminate in the rental of housing based on a tenant's or purchaser's source of lawful income, including lawful rent or mortgage payments such as a Section 8 HUD voucher.
coverage_conditions: Applies to the sale or rental of all property, business or residential, except an owner-occupied two-family dwelling's single apartment, a room rented in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling, religious-organization preference, and older-persons housing.

applicability.per_tenancy: Rental of a room or rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling; religious-organization preference; familial-status provision not applied to housing for older persons.
coverage_quotes: The rental of a single apartment or flat in a two-family dwelling, the other occupancy unit of which is occupied by the owner as his/her residence at the time of such rentals
The rental of a room or rooms to another person or persons by the owner or occupant of a one-family dwelling occupied by him/her as his/her residence at the time of such rental

exemptions: Single apartment in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling; rooms rented in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling; religious-organization preference to persons of the same religion; familial-status ban not applied to older-persons housing.
quoted_span: The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination based on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses. This means, for example, that a landlord cannot deny the lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful income.
